name: mkldnn_linear
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::mkldnn_linear(Tensor self, Tensor weight, Tensor? bias=None) -> Tensor. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, return values, errors, mutation and aliasing; tests are not narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: (1) "aten::mkldnn_linear.out(Tensor self, Tensor weight, Tensor? bias=None, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)"; (2) "aten::mkldnn_linear(Tensor self, Tensor weight, Tensor? bias=None) -> Tensor". Semantics derived from the tests: aten::mkldnn_linear is a CPU-only oneDNN inner product in which `self` is an opaque mkldnn activation tensor while `weight` (out_features, in_features) and optional `bias` (out_features,) are dense; the result is itself an opaque mkldnn tensor with the leading dimensions of `self` and the feature axis replaced by out_features. The public injected entrypoint exercised by the tests is flag_gems.mkldnn_linear(self, weight, bias) with the bias argument omissible, and flag_gems.mkldnn_linear(self, weight, bias, out=...) for the out= overload, which writes into the supplied keyword-only mkldnn out buffer, returns that same buffer (res_out is buf), and requires an mkldnn (not dense) out tensor. Candidates must not write into the operands. Supported activation dtypes are float32, float16, bfloat16, int8 and uint8; int8/uint8 have no oneDNN bias path, so those rows are bias-free, and to_mkldnn() rejects float64/int32/int64/bool/fp8. Backward requires FP32 weight/bias even for float16/bfloat16 activations, the activation gradient keeps the mkldnn layout while weight/bias gradients stay dense, and the upstream gradient must be an mkldnn tensor. Invalid operands (in_features mismatch, rank-1 weight, bias length mismatch) raise RuntimeError or TypeError. This definition models only the representative default overload; the out= overload's keyword-only out parameter and its mutation/aliasing behavior remain in the original pytest.
